name: Majority baseline
hypothesis: Sets the floor: balanced accuracy 0.500, recall 0, cost about 0.66 per wafer

name: LR, standardized
hypothesis: The sensors carry enough signal to beat the baseline, but extreme readings (up to 40 SD) make the risks overconfident

name: LR, quantile transform
hypothesis: Bounding extreme readings and removing skew gives honest risks, so the same threshold catches more failures at lower cost

name: Random forest, calibrated
hypothesis: Trees ignore scale and outliers and can combine sensors; if failures depend on combinations, the forest beats E3

name: LR, top-k sensors
hypothesis: Dropping the ~430 noise sensors helps the linear model

name: LR, L1 penalty
hypothesis: An L1 penalty picks a few sensors from groups of near-copies and generalises better than L2

name: Random forest, top-k sensors
hypothesis: Dropping the noise sensors lets the forest's splits find the useful ones

name: Random forest, tuned max_features
hypothesis: Letting each split see more sensors improves the forest's ranking

name: Average of E3 and E4
hypothesis: Linear and tree models make different errors, so their average beats both

name: Average of E5c and E6
hypothesis: Same, with the best variant of each family (optimistic: chosen on the same folds)

name: LR, quantile, detrended (W=200)
hypothesis: Removing sensor drift improves the late-wafer result of the linear model

name: Random forest, detrended (W=200)
hypothesis: Removing sensor drift fixes the forest's collapse on late wafers

name: LR, quantile, detrended (W=100)
hypothesis: Sensitivity check of the drift window

name: LR, quantile, detrended (W=400)
hypothesis: Sensitivity check of the drift window

name: Gradient boosting, calibrated
hypothesis: Shallow boosted trees capture sparse interactions better than a forest
